My role continues with regular performance tracking and analysis, to make sure we’re headed the right way, and I refine the strategy based on results to get the best possible return.

Because success in the digital world today doesn’t depend on being visible alone, but on staying present in your audience’s mind, and not being easy to forget.

From strategy to results: case studies

A real strategy shows its value when it turns into tangible results.

B2B landscape lighting

Ekhwa for Lighting

A brand with strong capabilities... but no results, and unknown in the market! How did I turn it into a distinguished brand in its field?

Ekhwa for Lighting is a brand specialized in landscape (Outdoor Lighting), targeting the B2B sector, especially large projects such as hotels, compounds, and real-estate development projects.

Objectives

  • Increase brand awareness
  • Precisely reach decision makers (lighting engineers, project managers, suppliers)
  • Achieve and increase sales

The situation

This is a landscape lighting brand, and on paper... everything was right:

  • High-quality materials
  • Warranties and periodic maintenance
  • Commitment to delivery

But reality was completely different... no sales, no results, and an almost total absence on social media.

I started with a comprehensive analysis of the current state (Content – Messaging – Positioning), until I reached a problem big enough to bring down any brand, however strong.

The real problem

The problem wasn’t in the product... It was that the brand couldn’t reach its audience. It didn’t know who it was talking to, what to say to them, or how to draw a clear picture of itself in the audience’s mind. This was because of:

  • Weak visual identity (it existed but didn’t reflect the brand’s strength)
  • No clear Positioning in the market
  • Random content with no strategy
  • Imprecise ad targeting, and therefore no results

Simply... a strong brand whose voice wasn’t reaching anyone. The solution wasn’t in the number of posts, but in setting a clear strategy.

The strategy

I built the strategy on 3 core pillars:

  • Repositioning the brand to reflect its real value in the market
  • Defining the Target Audience precisely and focusing on decision makers
  • A clear Content Direction that speaks directly to the audience’s needs

Then we started turning this into real execution:

  • A full Rebranding (Logo + Visual Identity) that reflects the brand’s level and target market
  • A targeted Content Plan combining Awareness – Educational – Sales
  • Launching ad campaigns, with continuous Testing to reach the most precise Target Audience

Every step was calculated... and that’s what began changing the results completely.

Results

150%+growth in qualified leads
200–250%higher conversion rates
450%+increase in reach

From a nearly stalled brand... to a brand competing strongly in its market. Simply... when the message arrived right, the results started to show.

B2C salad restaurant

Salad Fiesta

“Why should I pay all this money for a salad bowl?” That question was enough to bring down a brand... before it was even tried.

Salad Fiesta is a restaurant specialized in serving different kinds of salads, alongside complementary products such as fresh juices and fruit salad, and it targets the B2C sector.

Objectives

  • Increase sales
  • Increase branch visits
  • Reach the target audience precisely

The challenge

The common belief... is that salad is just a side dish. Not something you go to a restaurant for... or pay money for. But here... it was the Main Dish. And that was the real challenge.

  • A higher price than expected for a “salad” product
  • A mental barrier: “Why pay all this for a salad bowl?”
  • Difficulty communicating the brand’s value and menu variety
  • An incomplete picture in the customer’s mind

The traditional solution was obvious: sell the benefits of salad and that’s it... but that’s not what I did.

The approach

Because people already know its benefits... and still aren’t interested. So instead of selling “the benefit”... I decided to sell “the experience”.

I built a main Concept: “Not just a salad”, and presented the product as a Lifestyle, not just a meal. I started talking to each group in its own way:

  • Gen Z: try something different, stand out
  • Fitness Audience: a meal that supports your workout (energy + protein)
  • Mothers: a healthy choice for building better eating habits for children

Each group... a different message but the same goal, and that’s what began to change the audience’s reaction completely.

Execution

We turned the strategy into real execution:

  • Campaigns from different angles: (Not just a salad / A salad unlike any salad)
  • Varying messages by segment (Fitness – Gen Z – Mothers)
  • Highlighting product variety (juices – fruit salad – more options)
  • Improving ad targeting to reach each Segment with the right Message

Results

135–150%increase in branch visits
150–190%growth in direct orders via messages
Broke the price-related mental barrier and increased product acceptance

By the grace of God. When the idea was presented right, people started to get convinced... and to try.

Brand revival campaign

Saf Saf Restaurant

A restaurant that was number 1 in the market suddenly lost its audience and closed... The challenge: how do we get back to the top of the market?

Saf Saf is a restaurant serving a diverse selection of Eastern and Western food, and was once one of the best-known restaurants in its area.

Objectives

  • Erase the negative mental image of the restaurant
  • Win back old customers’ trust
  • Attract new customers
  • Achieve and increase sales
  • Build a strong social media presence

What happened

Saf Saf was one of the best-known restaurants in its area. A big audience... and trust built over years. But over time... all of that began to fade.

  • Lost touch with the new generation (Gen Z)
  • Forgot its old audience
  • Food quality and cleanliness suffered
  • Competition got stronger

The result? It lost people’s trust... and gained a negative reputation. Now the question: can a brand in this state... come back?

The real problem

The problem wasn’t just Marketing... it was deeper than that. The problems were in two directions:

  • Operational: food quality suffered; cleanliness standards weren’t consistent
  • Marketing: an unclear message; random content with no direction

It was clear that marketing alone wouldn’t solve the problem. So we started with what mattered most: improving food quality and committing to cleanliness standards. And after that... the real marketing work began.

The strategy

I built a strategy aimed at proving that the restaurant has really changed. From here the Concept came out: “Saf Saf: this time it’s different.” But the question was: how do we prove this to people... not just tell them? We started execution directly:

  • Reels from inside the restaurant (kitchen – preparation – cleanliness) to prove quality visually and authentically
  • Content focused on food Quality to rebuild the audience’s trust
  • A system executed with one clear core goal: restoring the restaurant’s true image

And gradually... the results started to show.

Results

250–300%jump in monthly orders
200%+improvement in engagement and mental image
150–200new customers every month

A large segment of old customers won back. I can say this was a successful Revival Campaign that brought back the trust and put the brand at the top of the market again.

Healthy children’s cereal, Iraqi market

Evocereal

How do you compete strongly in a market dominated by a product the whole audience has trusted for years?

Evocereal is a healthy breakfast cereal product for children in the Iraqi market, positioned as a natural alternative to imported products like Cerelac, and it targets mothers as Primary Decision Makers.

Objectives

  • Spread awareness of the product in the Iraqi market
  • Build a fan base among mothers
  • Position it as a trusted healthy choice for children
  • Compete with the market-dominant product

The challenges

  • Strong loyalty to an imported product (Cerelac)
  • Low awareness that a local alternative exists
  • Difficulty winning mothers’ trust in a product related to their children’s health
  • Building trust from zero in a very sensitive market

But the real challenge wasn’t the competitor... it was in the mother’s mind. To enter this market, we had to understand something more important than the product itself: what drives a mother’s decision? From here the shift began:

  • Focusing on the product’s core advantage (100% Natural, with no preservatives or sugar)
  • Addressing the fear motive around the child’s health, building gradual trust instead of direct selling

But there was one element that would determine the real success...

Execution

A competitor study to understand why people are attached to them and to offer a convincing alternative. Then I started executing on more than one level:

Content & Awareness

  • Educational content that explains the product’s benefits simply to mothers
  • Engagement Content to build trust and interaction

Trust Building

  • Using UGC (real experiences from mothers)
  • Continuous engagement to build a long-term relationship

Market Presence

  • Supporting the digital presence with Offline activities (nutrition Events)
  • Tailoring messages to the nature of the Iraqi audience

Every step aimed mainly at turning “a new product”... into “a trusted choice”.

Results

10,000+interested followers in a strong fan base
300%+growth in brand awareness in the Iraqi market
200%+improvement in trust and engagement
Wide spread of positive user experiences, strengthening product credibility

What made the difference: the trust that was built gradually turned a new product into a real choice in the market.

Content strategy redirection

Habitat Mattresses

How did I discover missed growth opportunities and redirect the content strategy for Habitat?

Habitat Mattresses is a brand specialized in mattresses, targeting different segments looking for comfort and sleep quality, with a focus on making the buying experience easier through fair prices, installment plans, and delivery services.

Objectives

  • Increase sales
  • Expand the target audience
  • Grow followers and improve engagement
  • Strengthen brand and product awareness

The situation

Habitat is a mattress brand, Saudi in origin and present in the Egyptian market. At the end of the winter season we noticed a big drop in sales, and the summer season was approaching. We had to pin down the real cause before starting any new moves. Is the problem in the ads? The content? Or the pricing and the way the product is presented?

I started by analyzing the last 3 months of performance and reviewing the current strategy, to get to the root of the problem and identify the growth opportunities we were missing.

The analysis

The problem wasn’t just a sales decline; we were also relying mainly on one segment: soon-to-be-married couples. This limited our chances of reaching other segments that need the product, such as:

  • Employees who suffer from discomfort during sleep
  • Older adults looking for comfort
  • Families renovating their home furniture
  • Families preparing their children’s rooms

Even within the target segment, we relied on limited marketing angles, like freedom of choice and trust in the product. The opportunity was in widening the audience, diversifying marketing messages, and linking the product to different needs.

The strategy

I started redirecting the strategy through 3 core pillars:

  • Widening target segments: reaching new audiences instead of relying on grooms and brides only
  • Diversifying marketing angles: developing messages that reflect each segment’s needs and buying motives
  • Highlighting the brand’s full value: Habitat’s advantages in prices, installment options, and ease of ordering and reaching the customer

From here the new campaign concept appeared: «Habitat Will Comfort You». Comfort isn’t just a comfortable mattress; it’s also in the buying experience, the ease of ordering, and the way we deal with customers. That gave us a broader concept to build multiple messages and campaigns on.

Execution

I turned the strategy into a clear execution plan:

  • Creative ideas tailored to each target segment
  • Each marketing message linked to the audience’s real needs and problems
  • Product advantages, offers, installments, and ease of purchase highlighted
  • Messages unified under the campaign concept «Habitat Will Comfort You»
  • Content directed to support sales, follower growth, and recovering engagement on the page

Instead of repeating the same message to everyone, each segment got a marketing entry point that suits it, while keeping the campaign’s core idea.

Results

  • Widened the target audience instead of relying on one segment
  • Developed new marketing angles that support presenting the brand’s value
  • Highlighted product advantages and the buying experience within one unified concept
  • Directed content to support sales, follower growth, and better engagement

The result was a more diverse content strategy, broader targeting, and marketing messages tied to different segments’ needs. The goal wasn’t simply to produce more content, but to address the causes of weak performance and build better growth opportunities.

Parenting and family-building platform

Benaat

How did an integrated content strategy help the Benaat platform regain its audience’s engagement, reach a new segment, and bring sales back?

Benaat is an educational platform specialized in providing courses for mothers in the field of parenting, expanded with the «Family Building» track to include people about to marry and the newly married.

Objectives

  • Restore the effectiveness of organic content
  • Strengthen brand awareness
  • Reach a new audience
  • Support sales and restore their growth

Challenges

  • A drop in sales after a period of better performance
  • The need to restore engagement rates and the effectiveness of organic content
  • Launching a new sign-language service and reaching its target audience
  • Developing content to keep pace with the platform’s expansion into family building

The core challenge: reactivating the platform, while widening its reach and developing how it communicates with its audience.

The plan

The action plan relied on 3 main pillars:

Reaching a new audience: designing a teaser campaign and then launching the sign-language-translated courses, relying on parenting situations close to the audience’s lives.

Developing the content experience: developing the existing programs and proposing new program ideas that support engagement and emotional connection with the brand.

Unifying messages: building a monthly thematic umbrella that connects parenting and family-building content in one integrated message instead of scattered topics.

Execution

Sign-language launch campaign: a campaign in two phases, teasing first through parenting situations and challenges, then revealing the sign-language-translated courses.

Developing existing programs: re-presenting the “My Mother Taught Me” series in two parts, to boost suspense and encourage the audience to follow the resolution.

Developing new programs: executing the first two programs from the proposed ideas to develop the content and strengthen communication with the audience.

Unifying content: applying a unified monthly concept that connects parenting and family topics within a cohesive editorial direction.

Results

  • Reach: reaching the deaf and hard-of-hearing audience and achieving the goal of introducing them to the platform
  • Engagement: restoring engagement rates and improving content performance
  • Brand awareness: strengthening awareness of the brand
  • Organic content: restoring its effectiveness and improving its performance
  • Sales: returning to making sales after the period of decline

Development didn’t stop at launching a new service; it extended to reviving content, widening reach, and supporting the return of sales.
